summary: Modern data platforms increasingly embed AI/ML capabilities directly where data lives, reducing the need to move data to external ML systems. Capabilities range from native vector search and semantic retrieval to in-database LLM access (via SQL functions) and traditional ML model training. With 75% of enterprise AI applications expected to depend on vector search by 2026 and vector database adoption growing 377% year over year, general-purpose databases are rapidly adding native vector and generative AI features to compete with purpose-built vector stores like Pinecone and Milvus.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.description: A fully managed service providing SQL and Python access to LLMs and ML functions. Cortex includes serverless LLM functions (COMPLETE, SUMMARIZE, TRANSLATE, SENTIMENT, EXTRACT_ANSWER), Cortex Search for RAG/semantic retrieval, Cortex Analyst for natural-language-to-SQL, and Document AI. It is also being brought to Snowflake Postgres, allowing Cortex AI functions to run against Postgres-managed data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Snowflake supports a VECTOR data type and vector similarity functions (VECTOR_COSINE_SIMILARITY, VECTOR_L2_DISTANCE, VECTOR_INNER_PRODUCT), plus Cortex Search for managed hybrid semantic search. No external extension required.
databases.llm_integration: Native, first-party hosted LLMs accessible via SQL/Python (Cortex COMPLETE function supports models from Anthropic, Meta Llama, Mistral, and Snowflake's own Arctic). No external API keys needed.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based pricing measured in Snowflake credits; Cortex LLM functions are billed per token processed, and vector/search operations consume compute credits. No separate licensing fee.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML with Vertex AI integration
databases.description: BigQuery ML lets users create and run ML models using standard SQL, including regression, classification, clustering, time-series forecasting, and anomaly detection. It integrates tightly with Vertex AI to call remote models (Gemini, embedding models) via ML.GENERATE_TEXT and ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING, enabling generative AI directly in SQL.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. BigQuery supports the VECTOR_SEARCH function and CREATE VECTOR INDEX for approximate nearest-neighbor search over embeddings stored in BigQuery tables.
databases.llm_integration: Deep native integration with Vertex AI and Gemini models via remote model functions (ML.GENERATE_TEXT, ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING, AI.GENERATE), callable from SQL.
databases.pricing_notes: Pay-per-query (on-demand bytes scanned) or capacity-based slot pricing; BigQuery ML has separate pricing for model creation and inference, and Vertex AI model calls incur Vertex AI charges.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.description: Open-source PostgreSQL gains AI capabilities through extensions: pgvector adds vector storage and similarity search, while pgai (from Timescale) brings embedding generation and LLM calls (OpenAI, Ollama, etc.) directly into SQL. Snowflake's AI-in-Postgres and pgai also enable in-database embedding and RAG workflows.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native to core PostgreSQL — vector search is provided only via the third-party pgvector extension, which adds the vector data type and HNSW/IVFFlat indexes. Without the extension, Postgres has no vector search.
databases.llm_integration: Via extensions such as pgai (embedding/completion functions) and pgvectorscale; LLM calls route to external providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, Cohere) configured by the user.
databases.pricing_notes: Core PostgreSQL and pgvector/pgai are open-source and free; costs are driven by self-hosting/compute or by managed Postgres providers plus any external LLM API usage.

databases.name: Amazon Aurora ML
databases.description: Aurora ML enables SQL-based inference by integrating Aurora (MySQL- and PostgreSQL-compatible) with Amazon SageMaker and Amazon Bedrock/Comprehend. Developers call ML models directly from SQL queries to add predictions, sentiment analysis, and generative AI responses without exporting data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Aurora ML itself does not provide native vector search. Aurora PostgreSQL supports vector search only through the pgvector extension, which is separate from the Aurora ML feature; Aurora MySQL relies on external services.
databases.llm_integration: Native integration with Amazon Bedrock (foundation models) and Amazon SageMaker/Comprehend callable from SQL, enabling LLM and ML inference inside Aurora queries.
databases.pricing_notes: No additional charge for the Aurora ML feature itself; you pay standard Aurora instance/storage/IO costs plus the underlying SageMaker, Bedrock, or Comprehend usage for inference.

databases.name: Amazon Redshift ML
databases.description: Redshift ML lets data analysts and scientists create, train, and deploy ML models using familiar SQL commands (CREATE MODEL), leveraging Amazon SageMaker Autopilot behind the scenes. It supports in-database prediction and integrates with Amazon Bedrock and SageMaker for generative AI and custom models.
databases.vector_search_notes: Redshift ML is focused on ML model training/inference, not vector search. Amazon Redshift has limited/emerging vector support, but Redshift ML itself does not provide native vector similarity search as a core capability.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon SageMaker (including bring-your-own-model and Autopilot) and Amazon Bedrock for LLM inference invoked via SQL.
databases.pricing_notes: Redshift ML uses SageMaker for training, which incurs SageMaker costs; prediction runs on Redshift compute. Standard Redshift node/serverless pricing applies plus SageMaker/Bedrock charges.

databases.name: Databricks (Mosaic AI + Vector Search)
databases.ai_feature: Mosaic AI and Databricks Vector Search
databases.description: Databricks Mosaic AI provides an end-to-end platform for building, fine-tuning, serving, and governing ML and generative AI models, including Model Serving, Agent Framework, and foundation model APIs. Databricks Vector Search is a serverless, managed vector database integrated with Unity Catalog for RAG applications.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Databricks Vector Search is a built-in, fully managed vector database that automatically syncs and indexes embeddings from Delta tables, governed by Unity Catalog.
databases.llm_integration: Native Foundation Model APIs and Model Serving provide access to hosted LLMs (Llama, DBRX, and external models), plus fine-tuning and agent orchestration via Mosaic AI.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based using Databricks Units (DBUs); Vector Search, Model Serving, and foundation model inference are billed separately based on compute and tokens, on top of cloud infrastructure costs.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.description: Atlas Vector Search enables storing embeddings alongside operational document data and running semantic similarity queries within the MongoDB aggregation pipeline. It supports hybrid search (combining vector and keyword/full-text) and powers RAG applications without a separate vector database.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Atlas Vector Search is a built-in capability using the $vectorSearch aggregation stage and Atlas Search indexes with ANN search; no external extension required.
databases.llm_integration: No first-party hosted LLMs; integrates via popular frameworks (LangChain, LlamaIndex) and external providers (OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI) for embedding generation and completions.
databases.pricing_notes: Available on MongoDB Atlas; vector search runs on dedicated Search Nodes or shared cluster resources, billed as part of Atlas cluster/compute pricing. External LLM/embedding API usage is separate.
